elements.element: Vendor must defend Customer against covered third-party claims.
elements.evidence: Section 9A.1 requires HDI to “defend” the Company against any covered third-party claim.

elements.element: Vendor must indemnify Customer against covered third-party claims and resulting losses.
elements.evidence: Section 9A.1 requires HDI to indemnify the Company for covered claims and resulting damages, costs, expenses, and reasonable attorneys’ fees.

elements.element: Customer’s affiliates must receive the Vendor defense and indemnity.
elements.evidence: Section 9A.1 expressly extends HDI’s defense and indemnity to the Company’s affiliates.

elements.element: Vendor indemnity must cover third-party allegations that the services or deliverables infringe or misappropriate intellectual property rights.
elements.evidence: Section 9A.1(a) covers allegations that HDI’s services, the Site, or other deliverables infringe or misappropriate any third party intellectual property right.

elements.element: Vendor indemnity must cover third-party claims arising from Vendor’s breach of applicable law.
elements.evidence: Section 9A.1(b) covers HDI’s breach of applicable law.

elements.element: Vendor indemnity must cover a data breach caused by Vendor.
elements.evidence: Section 9A.1(c) covers unauthorized access to or disclosure of Content caused by HDI, an operative formulation covering a Vendor-caused data breach.

elements.element: Vendor indemnity must cover third-party claims arising from Vendor’s gross negligence or willful misconduct.
elements.evidence: Section 9A.1(d) expressly covers HDI’s gross negligence or willful misconduct.

elements.element: The indemnification procedure must require prompt notice of a claim.
elements.evidence: Section 9A.3 requires the indemnified party to give prompt written notice.

elements.element: The indemnification procedure must give the indemnifying party control of the defense.
elements.evidence: Section 9A.3 requires the indemnified party to permit the indemnifying party to control the defense.

elements.element: The indemnification procedure must require reasonable cooperation.
elements.evidence: Section 9A.3 requires the indemnified party to provide reasonable cooperation.

elements.element: Customer’s indemnity must cover only third-party intellectual-property claims based on content or materials provided by Customer.
elements.evidence: Section 9A.2 covers third-party allegations that Content or Marks furnished by the Company infringe or misappropriate intellectual property rights.

elements.element: Customer’s indemnity may cover Customer’s breach of applicable law.
elements.evidence: Section 9A.2 covers the Company’s breach of applicable law.

elements.element: Customer must have no indemnity obligations beyond Customer-provided content or materials and Customer’s breach of applicable law.
elements.evidence: Section 9A.2 contains no additional Company indemnity triggers beyond furnished Content or Marks and the Company’s breach of applicable law.

elements.element: Vendor must indemnify Customer against third-party intellectual-property claims concerning the services or deliverables.
elements.evidence: Section 9A.1(a) provides this indemnity and also includes a defense obligation.

elements.element: The Vendor IP indemnity must exclude infringement caused by Customer modifications.
elements.evidence: No exclusion for modifications made by or on behalf of the Company appears in the rendered clause.

elements.element: The Vendor IP indemnity must exclude infringement caused by combinations with items not supplied or approved by Vendor.
elements.evidence: No combination exclusion appears in the rendered clause.

elements.element: The Vendor IP indemnity must exclude infringement resulting from Customer-provided specifications.
elements.evidence: No exclusion for compliance with Company specifications appears in the rendered clause.

elements.element: The Vendor IP remedy must permit or require Vendor to procure continued lawful use.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause contains no obligation to procure continued use rights.

elements.element: The Vendor IP remedy must permit or require Vendor to modify the affected services or deliverables to become non-infringing.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause contains no modification remedy.

elements.element: The Vendor IP remedy must permit or require Vendor to replace the affected services or deliverables with non-infringing substitutes.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause contains no replacement remedy.

elements.element: The Vendor IP remedy must provide a refund if continued use, modification, or replacement is unavailable.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause contains no refund remedy.

elements.element: Vendor’s indemnity liability must be subject to a super-cap equal to 3× annual fees.
elements.evidence: No indemnity cap or 3× annual-fees super-cap appears in the rendered clause.

result.reason: The operative language satisfies every preferred requirement: HDI defends and indemnifies the Company and its affiliates for the specified third-party claim categories, the required procedure is included, and the Company’s indemnity is narrowly confined. The fallback is not satisfied because its modification, combination, and specification exclusions, its procure/modify/replace/refund remedies, and its 3× annual-fees super-cap are all absent. The change is substantively focused and does not disturb the existing commercial language, although placing section 9A after the section 10 heading is a minor numbering/placement defect.
